name: object-storage-s3
description: Bun-native S3-compatible object storage for AWS S3 or MinIO-compatible services with a StorageService and presigned URLs.

inject.text:
### object-storage-s3
- Store files through `OBJECT_STORAGE` from `@podosoft/podokit-runtime` (`services.resolve(OBJECT_STORAGE)`), not the provider directly. `put(key, body, { contentType })` streams a `ReadableStream` such as `request.body`, a `Blob` or file, an async iterable, bytes, or a string without buffering it; a failed body leaves no partial object.
- For uploads split across requests (resumable or chunked), use `createMultipartUpload`, `uploadPart` (parts numbered 1 to 10,000, each but the last at least `MIN_MULTIPART_PART_BYTES` = 5 MiB), `completeMultipartUpload`, and `abortMultipartUpload`. Branch on `MultipartUploadError.code` (`UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_PART`, `PART_TOO_SMALL`).
- Multipart requests are signed with the `S3_*` (or `AWS_*`) credentials. A part passed as a stream is held in memory while it is sent, so keep parts to tens of MiB. On AWS, add an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` bucket lifecycle rule.

instructions: Start Silo for local dev:  docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml -f infra/docker/minio.compose.yml up -d
The /storage demo routes need the auth module and an administrator session, and only reach keys under demo/.
Sign in as an administrator:  curl -c cookies.txt -XPOST localhost:5002/api/auth/sign-in/email -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"<password>"}'
Store an object:  curl -b cookies.txt -XPUT localhost:5002/storage/hello -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"content":"hi"}'
Read it back:     curl -b cookies.txt localhost:5002/storage/hello
For AWS S3: set STORAGE_PROVIDER=aws, remove S3_ENDPOINT, set S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=false and real credentials/bucket.
OBJECT_STORAGE.put streams large or streamed bodies as a multipart upload; uploads split across requests use createMultipartUpload, uploadPart, completeMultipartUpload, and abortMultipartUpload.
On AWS, add a bucket lifecycle rule with AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload so abandoned multipart uploads are removed.
